t.1.98.1: Bhīṣma said: O greatly fortunate lady, Rāma Jāmadagnya, unable to bear the slaying of his father and filled with wrath, slew the lord of the Haihayas; the thousand arms of Arjuna were indeed cut off.
t.1.98.2: And again, taking up his bow and loosing mighty weapons, conquering the earth with his chariot, he burned down the kṣatriya race again and again.
t.1.98.3: Thus in former times, with weapons high and low, the great-souled Bhārgava made the earth empty of kṣatriyas thrice seven times.
t.1.98.4: Then everywhere, all the Kṣatriya women, uniting with self-restrained Brāhmaṇas, had offspring begotten by them.
t.1.98.5: It is settled in the Vedas that a son belongs to the one who took the mother's hand in marriage; keeping this law in mind, those women approached the brahmins. In the world too, this rebirth of the kṣatriyas is seen to have been practised.
t.1.98.6: Now, in former times there was a wise seer known as Utathya. He had a wife named Mamatā, whom he held in the highest esteem.
t.1.98.7: But Utathya's younger brother, Bṛhaspati of great splendor, the household priest of the dwellers of heaven, approached Mamatā.
t.1.98.8: But Mamatā said to him, her brother-in-law, the best of speakers: "I am pregnant by your elder brother; desist!"
t.1.98.11: Though thus properly addressed by her, Bṛhaspati of great splendour was then unable to restrain himself, whose very self was given over to desire.
t.1.98.9: And this son of Utathya, O illustrious Bṛhaspati, while still in my womb, has learned the Veda with its six limbs right here.
t.1.98.10: And you too must surely be one whose seed never fails; therefore, matters being as they are, you should desist today.
t.1.98.12: Then, filled with desire, he united with her, though she was unwilling; but as he was releasing his seed, the one dwelling in the womb spoke to him.
t.1.98.14: Addressed thus, the blessed seer Bṛhaspati became enraged; then, after rebuking the son of Utathya who was still in the womb, he cursed him.
t.1.98.13: Ho, dear younger one, I tell you, there is no room here for two; your seed is unfailing, and I came here first.
t.1.98.16: Because of the curse, he was born as the seer named Dīrghatamas, son of the greatly renowned Bṛhaspati, and he was like Bṛhaspati himself in vigor.
t.1.98.17: Then that greatly renowned one begot sons, Gautama and the others, for the increase of the lineage and family of the seer Utathya.
t.1.98.15: Since you speak such words to me at a time like this, a moment longed for by all beings, you shall therefore enter a long darkness.
t.1.98.18: Overcome by greed and delusion, those sons, Gautama and the others, placed him in a wooden chest and cast him adrift on the Gaṅgā.
t.1.98.20: Then, O king, that blind seer, floating downstream on that raft, travelled through a great many lands.
t.1.98.19: "This man, blind and old, should not have to be supported," so they thought; and then those cruel ones went back to their homes.
t.1.98.21: But a king named Bali, learned in all the laws of dharma, who had gone to bathe, saw him carried near by the current.
t.1.98.23: For the sake of offspring, O illustrious one, O giver of honor, you should beget upon my wives sons skilled in dharma and artha.
t.1.98.22: Bali, the righteous-souled king of true valor, caught hold of him, and having recognized who he was, he then chose him for the sake of a son, O bull among men.
t.1.98.24: Thus addressed, the radiant seer said to him, "So be it." Then the king sent to him his own wife, Sudeṣṇā.
t.1.98.25: Considering him to be blind and old, that queen did not go to him; instead she then sent her own foster-sister to that old man.
t.1.98.26: On her, a woman of śūdra birth, that self-controlled seer of righteous soul begot eleven sons, Kākṣīvant and the others.
t.1.98.27: Seeing all those sons, Kākṣīvat and the others, engaged in their studies, the mighty king said to that ṛṣi, "These are mine."
t.1.98.28: "No," the great seer said to him, declaring, "these are mine alone, for it was by me that these sons, Kākṣīvat and the others, were begotten in a śūdra womb."
t.1.98.29: Thinking me blind and old, your chief queen Sudeṣṇā, deluded, scorned me and gave me a Śūdra woman, her foster-sister.
t.1.98.30: Then Bali once more propitiated that best of seers, and he sent his wife Sudeṣṇā to him again.
t.1.98.31: Then Dīrghatamas, having touched that queen on her limbs, said to her, "You will have a son, radiant and truthful in speech."
t.1.98.32: There the royal seer named Aṅga was born of Sudeṣṇā. In this way other kṣatriyas, great archers, were begotten on earth by brāhmaṇas.
t.1.98.33: were born, men who knew the highest dharma, valorous and of great strength. Having heard this, mother, you too do here as you wish.
